applications.name: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: posterior spinal fusion
applications.why_biologic: Synthetic ceramic extends or partly replaces iliac crest and local bone in long instrumented fusions, where autograft volume is the limit.
applications.autograft_standard: Local spinous-process and rib bone plus iliac crest autograft or allograft; the downside is limited volume and donor-site pain.
applications.volume_note: Not sourced: no public US procedure-volume figure with a citable source was located in this sweep.

applications.name: Knee subchondral bone marrow lesion (BML) with osteoarthritis: percutaneous subchondral calcium phosphate injection (Subchondroplasty)
applications.why_biologic: Injectable calcium phosphate is placed into the painful BML to fill microtrabecular defects and restore subchondral support; it is a joint-preserving, not a fusion or fracture, use.
applications.autograft_standard: No bone-graft standard; the alternatives are NSAIDs, injections, bisphosphonates, activity change and eventually arthroplasty.
applications.volume_note: Not sourced: no public US procedure-volume figure with a citable source was located in this sweep.

applications.name: Benign bone cyst or tumor (for example unicameral bone cyst, enchondroma): curettage and void filling
applications.why_biologic: After curettage the cavity is filled with a resorbable osteoconductive material in place of autograft or allograft.
applications.autograft_standard: Autologous iliac crest or local cancellous graft, or allograft chips; the downside is donor-site pain in children and limited volume.
applications.volume_note: Not sourced: no public US procedure-volume figure with a citable source was located in this sweep.

applications.name: Prophylactic local augmentation of the osteoporotic proximal femur (fragility-fracture prevention)
applications.why_biologic: A resorbable triphasic implant is injected into the femoral neck and trochanter to form new bone locally, aiming to cut the risk of a second hip fracture faster than drug therapy.
applications.autograft_standard: No graft standard; systemic osteoporosis drugs take months to lower hip-fracture risk.
applications.volume_note: Not sourced: no public US procedure-volume figure with a citable source was located in this sweep.

products.name: Pro Osteon (200 / 200R / 500 / 500R coralline hydroxyapatite)
products.ownership_history: Developed by Interpore International (Irvine, CA); the Pro Osteon 500R 2007 summary names Biomet Osteobiologics; Zimmer Biomet since the 2015 Zimmer-Biomet merger. Acquisition dates not re-sourced.
products.composition: Coral-derived porous hydroxyapatite blocks and granules (the Interpore coralline line): Pro Osteon 200 is coral converted to hydroxyapatite; Pro Osteon 500/500R is a coral-carbonate skeleton with a thin calcium phosphate surface layer that resorbs faster (composition per a 2019 marine-materials review; not re-checked against the IFU).

regulatory.reference: K063346 (Pro Osteon 500R, expanded indications, April 2007); earlier K980817 and K990131 (500R), K000515 (200R), K004003 (200R with calcium sulfate)
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for bony voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure, gently packed into the skeletal system 'extremities, spine and pelvis' (K063346)
Surgically created or traumatic osseous defects; may be combined with autogenous bone marrow aspirate, autogenous blood or sterile fluids
A secondary IFU listing reports contraindications for growth-plate fractures, segmental defects and infected sites (IFU not read in full)

applications.evidence_summary: Bucholz 1989 (PMID 2537166): metaphyseal defects in 40 displaced tibial plateau fractures were filled with cancellous autograft or interporous hydroxyapatite (the Interpore 200 material that became Pro Osteon); no significant radiographic or clinical difference at 15 to 34 months. A 2013 review of tibial plateau graft substitutes (PMID 23351879) found hydroxyapatite step-off at follow-up of 2 mm or more in 5.4%.
applications.caveats: Allocation method is not stated and follow-up differed (15.4 vs 34.5 months); 1989 fixation and imaging standards; the product tested is the older Interpore 200, not the 2007 500R label.

applications.evidence_summary: Interpore coralline hydroxyapatite mixed about 70/30 with iliac autograft in 27 consecutive adolescent idiopathic scoliosis posterior fusions: all achieved solid fusion at 27 months average (PMID 12401014).
applications.caveats: Single-center case series without a control; 2002; coral material from the Interpore era.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Pro Osteon lumbar posterolateral fusion; coralline hydroxyapatite spine fusion).
applications.caveats: Label covers spine; Zimmer Biomet registered an observational Pro Osteon study (NCT00858598) that was withdrawn with zero enrollment.

evidence.title: Interporous hydroxyapatite as a bone graft substitute in tibial plateau fractures
evidence.finding: Metaphyseal defects filled with interporous hydroxyapatite or cancellous autograft showed no significant difference in radiographic or clinical results.

evidence.title: Supplementation of autogenous bone graft with coralline hydroxyapatite in posterior spine fusion for idiopathic adolescent scoliosis
evidence.finding: All 27 patients had solid fusion at an average 27 months using coralline hydroxyapatite mixed with limited iliac autograft.

evidence.title: Use of bone graft substitutes in the management of tibial plateau fractures
evidence.finding: Systematic review reports hydroxyapatite and calcium phosphate cement substitutes with low rates of secondary articular depression and no good-quality RCTs for graft substitutes.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Mature, low-visibility line in the Zimmer Biomet biologics catalog; presence in the current catalog was not confirmed on a company page (GUDID lists device identifiers). Coral-derived raw material is a supply and diligence topic.

products.name: AccuFill Bone Substitute Material (Subchondroplasty procedure)
products.ownership_history: Knee Creations (Subchondroplasty originator) became part of Zimmer Biomet; the 510(k) applicant is named Zimmer Knee Creations. Acquisition year not re-sourced.
products.composition: Injectable, self-setting, macroporous, osteoconductive calcium phosphate bone graft substitute (per 510(k) indications text); delivered through the Subchondroplasty instrument set.

regulatory.reference: K190814 (June 2019, applicant Zimmer Knee Creations)
on_label_indications: Injectable, self-setting, macroporous, osteoconductive calcium phosphate bone graft substitute to fill bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system of the extremities, spine (posterolateral spine) and pelvis that are not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure
Surgically created osseous defects or defects from traumatic injury; resorbs and is replaced by bone

applications.evidence_summary: Zimmer-sponsored prospective single-arm cohort of 70 knees treated with AccuFill showed significant pain and KOOS gains through 24 months, with 76.2% arthroplasty-free survival at 2 years (PMID 39667406); a 92-knee European multicenter study reports 91.5% surgery-free at 24 months (PMID 42673584); a 2026 meta-analysis of 12 mostly non-randomized studies (829 patients) found clinically important pain and function gains (PMID 41950892).
applications.caveats: All sponsor-linked or uncontrolled; the Zimmer Biomet Subchondroplasty randomized trial (NCT03112200, n=131, completed 2023, results posted) has no peer-reviewed publication located in PubMed on 2026-10-23.
applications.challenge: The cleared indication reads as bone void or gap filling in extremities, spine and pelvis; bone marrow lesion treatment is not named in the indications text read. A hiring manager will ask where the on-label line sits for Subchondroplasty in osteoarthritic knees.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: AccuFill tibial plateau; Subchondroplasty tibial plateau fracture).
applications.caveats: Used for subchondral support in some centers; no AccuFill-specific fracture series located.

evidence.title: Prospective Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes of the Subchondroplasty Procedure for Treatment of Symptomatic Bone Marrow Lesions of the Knee
evidence.finding: Pain and KOOS improved significantly through 24 months; 76.2% avoided arthroplasty at 2 years.

evidence.title: Calcium-Phosphate Subchondroplasty Provides Durable 24-Month Pain Relief and >90% Surgery-free Survivorship for Tibiofemoral Bone Marrow Lesions in Mild-To-Moderate Knee Osteoarthritis: A Prospective Multicenter Study
evidence.finding: Large, durable pain and function gains with 91.5% surgery-free survivorship at 24 months and 7.6% reoperation.

evidence.title: Subchondroplasty for bone-marrow lesions in the osteoarthritic knee improves pain and function: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Twelve studies showed clinically important pain and function improvement from one month to two years, with 3.5% reoperation.

evidence.title: Subchondroplasty Knee RCT (Zimmer Biomet)
evidence.finding: Randomized trial of Subchondroplasty plus arthroscopy versus arthroscopy alone, completed August 2023 with registry results posted; peer-reviewed publication not located.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Procedure-driven franchise (Subchondroplasty) sold through Zimmer Biomet's knee preservation sales force; payer coverage of the procedure itself varies.

products.name: AttraX Putty and AttraX Scaffold
products.ownership_history: Progentix Orthobiology (Bilthoven, NL) originated AttraX/Curios; NuVasive held the AttraX clearances from 2017 (K172497); Globus Medical completed its NuVasive merger in September 2023 (merger date from public record, not re-sourced).
products.composition: Synthetic biphasic calcium phosphate ceramic granules with a needle-like surface topography (Progentix/Curios technology): the Putty is ceramic granules premixed with a polymeric binder; the Scaffold is a moldable strip form.

regulatory.reference: K191974 (AttraX Putty, Nov 2019); K240507 (AttraX Scaffold, March 2024); K172497 (Scaffold, 2017); original K151584 (AttraX Putty, Progentix Orthobiology, Oct 2015)
on_label_indications: AttraX Putty (K191974): implant to fill bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'posterolateral spine and pelvis', may be used in combination with autogenous bone; resorbs and is replaced with bone

AttraX Scaffold (K240507): posterolateral spine, intervertebral disc space and pelvis; in the posterolateral spine must be used with autogenous bone or bone marrow aspirate; in intervertebral body fusion must be used with a cage cleared for use with a bone void filler
Globus's website also states a Putty interbody indication; the 510(k) supporting it was not located (unverified)

applications.evidence_summary: Dutch multicenter, intrapatient-controlled noninferiority RCT (n=100 enrolled, 87 analysed, 146 instrumented segments): 1-year PLF rate 55% AttraX Putty vs 52% autograft side, difference 2.3% (90% CI -9.1 to 13.7), noninferior (PMID 32080013); at 2 years 70% vs 68%, no difference (PMID 32459724).
applications.caveats: Fusion rates of 52 to 55% at one year are low in absolute terms (CT-based); intrapatient design with local bone in all segments; a published erratum exists (PMID 34183620); conflicts disclosed in the paper were not individually reviewed.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: AttraX Putty interbody OR TLIF OR PLIF).
applications.caveats: On-label only for AttraX Scaffold with an FDA-cleared cage for use with a bone void filler; in the Dutch RCT 62% of patients also had an interbody procedure but the graft under test was posterolateral.

applications.evidence_summary: NuVasive registered a randomized AttraX Putty versus autograft XLIF trial (NCT02250248, n=45, completed May 2021); no peer-reviewed results were located.
applications.caveats: Registry-only evidence; sponsor-run. Putty label (K191974) does not name interbody; the Scaffold label does.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: AttraX pelvis; AttraX acetabular).
applications.caveats: Pelvis is named in both labels; no product-specific pelvic series located.

evidence.title: Efficacy of a Standalone Microporous Ceramic Versus Autograft in Instrumented Posterolateral Spinal Fusion: A Multicenter, Randomized, Intrapatient Controlled, Noninferiority Trial
evidence.finding: AttraX Putty fusion 55% vs autograft 52% at 1 year, noninferior within a 15% margin.

evidence.title: Increasing Fusion Rate Between 1 and 2 Years After Instrumented Posterolateral Spinal Fusion and the Role of Bone Grafting
evidence.finding: Fusion rose to 70% (AttraX Putty) and 68% (autograft) at 2 years with no difference between grafts.

evidence.title: AttraX Putty vs. Autograft in XLIF (NuVasive)
evidence.finding: Registered randomized comparison of AttraX Putty and autograft in lateral interbody fusion; completed, no published results located.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Strongest-evidenced synthetic in this slice: only one with a published Level I PLF noninferiority RCT. Globus markets it with its own spine implant franchise.

regulatory.reference: K241167 (BioSphere Putty and MIS, Dec 2024); K173301 (MIS, 2018); K173424 (Flex, Sept 2018); K140844 (July 2014); K122868 (April 2013)

products.name: Bongros-HA / Bongros-GS (Korea)
products.ownership_history: CGBio (formerly Novomedics, Korea) also owns the Novosis rhBMP-2 record already in the atlas; Bioalpha as CGBio's subsidiary or partner is not confirmed.

evidence.title: A prospective consecutive study of instrumented posterolateral lumbar fusion using synthetic hydroxyapatite (Bongros-HA) as a bone graft extender

products.name: Herafill (gentamicin calcium sulfate / calcium carbonate beads and granules)
products.ownership_history: Heraeus Medical (part of the Heraeus group, Hanau/Wehrheim, Germany).
products.composition: Biconvex 6 mm beads or granules of calcium sulfate and calcium carbonate with about 1% gentamicin sulfate and glycerol tripalmitate as binder: a resorbable synthetic antibiotic carrier.

regulatory.reference: CE-marked (market entry 2010 per a clinical paper); no FDA 510(k) or PMA found in openFDA (searched device name 'herafill')
on_label_indications: CE-marked ex-US as a gentamicin-loaded resorbable bone void filler; no FDA indication exists

applications.evidence_summary: No published controlled study of Herafill in osteomyelitis dead space located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Herafill osteomyelitis). Preclinical data: three-way sheep comparison of gentamicin-loaded Stimulan-G, Cerament-G and Herafill-G (PMID 32840717) and a rat Masquelet granule-size study (PMID 31721435); Herafill was one of the carriers used in a periprosthetic joint infection DAIR cohort of mixed carriers (PMID 31321457).
applications.caveats: Not authorized in the US; in the 12-sheep comparison Herafill-G showed the lowest bone gain of the three carriers; elution and bone data are animal-only.
applications.challenge: The sheep-model finding should not be quoted as human comparative efficacy.

evidence.title: Comparative osteoconductivity of bone void fillers with antibiotics in a critical size bone defect model
evidence.finding: In sheep, Stimulan-G and Cerament-G produced similar bone gains while Herafill-G showed the lowest increases in bone volume and surface area, similar to negative-control sites.

evidence.title: Size matters: Effect of granule size of the bone graft substitute (Herafill) on bone healing using Masquelet's induced membrane in a critical size defect model in the rat's femur
evidence.finding: Three Herafill granule sizes, with or without bone marrow cells, were compared in a 10 mm rat femoral defect with an induced membrane.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable in the US (not marketed).

products.name: OsteoFlo NanoPutty, HydroPutty and HydroFiber
products.ownership_history: SurGenTec, LLC (Boca Raton, FL); privately held, no acquirer found.
products.composition: Fully synthetic hydrophilic grafts: NanoPutty is quadphasic particles (hydroxyapatite, alpha-TCP, beta-TCP, bioactive glass) in a bioresorbable polymer binder; HydroPutty is carbonated apatite granules and bioglass in a synthetic polymer binder; HydroFiber is the fibrous form. regulatory.reference: K251720 (OsteoFlo HydroFiber, July 2025, summary not retrievable); K243949 (HydroFiber, May 2025); K242797 (HydroFiber, Dec 2024); K231716 (HydroPutty, Oct 2023); K200064 (NanoPutty, Aug 2020)
on_label_indications: HydroFiber (K243949): bone void filler for osseous defects not intrinsic to stability, packed into the 'extremities, pelvis, intervertebral disc space, and posterolateral spine'; standalone or with autograft as an extender; in intervertebral body fusion must be used with a cage cleared for a bone void filler

applications.evidence_summary: Retrospective chart review of 129 patients (211 lateral mass and 199 interbody fusions) using OsteoFlo mixed with a cellular allograft (Vimax): Bridwell grade I fusion 77.8% of lateral-mass and 92.0% of interbody levels at 1 year (PMID 40242813).
applications.caveats: No control group; the product used (2021 to 2022) was the NanoPutty/HydroPutty generation whose labels named extremities and pelvis only, so the spine use then was off-label; mixed with a cellular allograft, so the effect of the synthetic alone is not isolated.

applications.evidence_summary: Same series: 92.0% Bridwell I fusion at 1 year across 199 interbody levels (PMID 40242813). A 2026 case report used stand-alone HydroFiber-type graft in a postoperative osteomyelitis/discitis salvage (PMID 42724889); a rabbit PLF study showed noninferiority to iliac autograft (PMID 42003666).
applications.caveats: Interbody label requires a cage cleared for bone void filler use; case report and animal study are not clinical evidence of equivalence.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: OsteoFlo tibial plateau OR extremity).
applications.caveats: Extremities now named for HydroFiber (May 2025).

evidence.title: Rate of fusion using novel synthetic bone graft mixed with cellular allograft product in lumbar fusions
evidence.finding: Bridwell grade I fusion at 1 year was 77.8% (lateral mass) and 92.0% (interbody) with OsteoFlo plus a cellular allograft.

evidence.title: A Novel Nano-Synthetic Hydrophilic Bone Graft (OsteoFlo HydroFiber) Is a Non-inferior Alternative to Iliac Crest Autograft in a Rabbit Posterolateral Fusion Model
evidence.finding: In rabbits, HydroFiber was noninferior to iliac crest autograft for posterolateral fusion.

products.name: HEALOS and HEALOS Fx (collagen-hydroxyapatite sponge)
products.ownership_history: Orquest, Inc. originated HEALOS; acquired by DePuy Spine (J&J) and now under DePuy Synthes. Acquisition date not sourced.
products.composition: Collagen-ceramic composite: bovine Type I collagen fibers coated with hydroxyapatite (about 30% mineral by weight); soaked in the patient's bone marrow aspirate; Fx is an injectable form with a mixing and delivery system.

regulatory.reference: K081758 (HEALOS Fx, Sept 2008); K062495 (Fx, 2006); K043308 (modification, 2005); K012751 (HEALOS, Nov 2001, Orquest)
on_label_indications: HEALOS Fx combined with autogenous bone marrow: filling bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'extremities, spine, and pelvis' not intrinsic to stability; surgically created or traumatic defects; resorbed and remodeled into new bone (K081758)
Separate dental and Healos II clearances exist (K081432, K093390; product code LYC)

products.challenge: Off-market status is inferred, not confirmed; the interbody RCT NCT00316121 is unpublished.

applications.evidence_summary: Neen 2006 (PMID 16915079): Healos plus bone marrow aspirate in 50 matched lumbar fusions versus historical iliac autograft controls: equivalent radiographic and clinical results in posterolateral fusion, no persisting donor-site complications versus 14% in autograft. Counterpoints: Ploumis 2010 (PMID 20672956; n=28 degenerative scoliosis) found equal clinical outcome but slower fusion than allograft, and a Thai intrapatient series (PMID 23991599; n=27) found 2-year radiographic fusion 29.6% with Healos/BMA versus 63.0% with local graft.
applications.caveats: Mixed evidence; historical controls in Neen; older 2000s imaging standards; outcomes depend on bone marrow aspirate quality.

applications.evidence_summary: Neen 2006: radiographic fusion rate was significantly lower with Healos in interbody fusions despite similar clinical outcomes. Case series of 20 TLIF/PLF patients: 95% fusion at 27 months (PMID 19111510). DePuy-linked randomized TLIF trial of Healos versus autograft (NCT00316121, n=138, completed, results posted) has no peer-reviewed report located.
applications.caveats: The registered randomized trial would be the strongest dataset but was not found in PubMed on 2026-10-23.
applications.challenge: Interbody data are mixed and the RCT is unpublished; a hiring manager would ask why.

applications.evidence_summary: Ploumis 2010 (PMID 20672956): Healos graft carrier with bone marrow aspirate plus local autograft (n=12) versus cancellous allograft plus local autograft (n=16) in degenerative lumbar scoliosis PLF: similar 2-year clinical results, Healos fusion slower.
applications.caveats: Small retrospective grouping.

evidence.title: Healos and bone marrow aspirate used for lumbar spine fusion: a case controlled study comparing healos with autograft
evidence.finding: Equivalent fusion in posterolateral lumbar fusion versus matched historical autograft, but significantly lower radiographic fusion in lumbar interbody fusions.

evidence.title: Healos graft carrier with bone marrow aspirate instead of allograft as adjunct to local autograft for posterolateral fusion in degenerative lumbar scoliosis: a minimum 2-year follow-up study
evidence.finding: Equal pain, function, curve and fusion rates at 2 years, but earlier fusion with allograft than with Healos.

evidence.title: A comparative study of radiographic results using HEALOS collagen-hydroxyapatite sponge with bone marrow aspiration versus local bone graft in the same patients undergoing posterolateral lumbar fusion
evidence.finding: Radiographic fusion at 2 years was 29.6% on the Healos side versus 63.0% on the local-bone side.

evidence.title: Clinical and radiographic assessment of transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion using HEALOS collagen-hydroxyapatite sponge with autologous bone marrow aspirate
evidence.finding: Overall fusion 95% (21 of 22 levels) at an average 27 months.

products.name: AGN1 (JGH1) injectable triphasic calcium-based bone graft substitute, Local Osteo-Enhancement Procedure (LOEP)
products.composition: Resorbable triphasic calcium-based implant material, injected as a paste that cures in situ; used for LOEP in the osteoporotic proximal femur.

regulatory.reference: K181342 (JGH1 Bone Graft Substitute, July 2018); K181585 (JGH1 Core Decompression Procedure Kit, July 2018). Link between the 'JGH1' 510(k) name and the 'AGN1' name used in publications is assumed, not sourced.

products.name: Agilon Moldable / Agilon Strip and Morpheus (osteoSPAN granule bone grafts)
products.composition: osteoSPAN granules (about 65% porous biphasic calcium salts, primarily calcium carbonate with a thin calcium phosphate layer; origin not stated in the text read, a coral-type structure is implied by the description) suspended in an organic binder; Agilon Strip adds collagen.

regulatory.reference: K240621 (Morpheus Moldable / Agilon Moldable, April 2024, summary not retrievable); K193487 (Agilon Strip, March 2020); K193168 (Agilon Moldable, Feb 2020); K190371 (Morpheus-C, 2019)
on_label_indications: Agilon Moldable and Strip (K193168, K193487): voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'extremities, pelvis, and posterolateral spine' not intrinsic to stability; alone in the extremities and pelvis, but must be mixed with autograft in the posterolateral spine

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Agilon OR osteoSPAN OR Biogennix posterolateral fusion). A 2024 materials paper characterized an osteoSPAN-type nanocrystalline hydroxycarbonapatite graft (PMID 38747324).
applications.caveats: Materials characterization only.
